text:
maria: Hey team — spotted a weird $98.40 charge on my corp card from 'AIRPORT-RIDE' while I was waiting at SFO yesterday. I attached the receipt but it only shows a flat total, no itemization. Is surge accepted on corpcard?
lee (Finance): Hi Maria — thanks for flagging. We need an itemized receipt showing fare + surge breakdown or a driver/vendor note. If that's not available, manager approval can be accepted as an exception for audit.
maria: Uploaded the PDF here: https://files.company/receipts/2051234567-sfo-ride.pdf. It literally says "Total: $98.40" and merchant code RIDE-SVC. No breakdown anywhere.
sarah (Manager): I approve the exception for Maria for this SFO trip. Business reason: onsite customer kickoff and a flight delay caused ~45min wait for alternative transport. @lee (Finance) — ok to process? :thumbsup:
lee (Finance): Thanks @sarah. Please reply with the single word "approved" so we keep a text record in the thread for audit. Maria — also file the expense in Expensify with project code RW-ONBOARD and attach both the PDF and a screenshot of this thread.
maria: approved. Filing now. Quick question: is the surge portion VAT-reclaimable for our UK entity? This was a US ride but wondering for future EU trips.
lee (Finance): For US domestic rides, VAT/GST generally doesn't apply, so nothing to reclaim. If you have EU rides with VAT shown on an invoice, upload that invoice and tag it "VAT" in Expensify and we will evaluate reclaim eligibility.
expensify-bot: Expense created (ID: 342-205123) by maria for $98.40, status: submitted.
lee (Finance): Got it — we'll mark this as an approved exception and reimburse once Expensify moves it to approved. Note for records: manager approval captured in thread. Closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
